Both setups use an arbitrary finite global lower bound, not an attained minimizer. The analytic iteration theorem accepts that same kind of lower bound.

The actual setup reuses IID for tape coordinates with common marginal and independence. Fresh-sample integration uses prefix-tail independence; the independent algorithm selector is separately represented by the product law.

The existing IsStochasticGradient structure enforces integrable gradients and their vector expectation equal to the true gradient at every point. Its actual type contains no convexity/minimizer assumption despite its module name.
That same inspected structure bounds the centered squared-gradient integral by sigma squared; oracle_moments and iterate_moments propagate the required second moments and integrability.
The timing invariant and delays_bound identify a_k as the assignment index, so 0<=k-a_k<R on the existing event prefix. The implementation does not confuse a_k itself with the delay.
Actual initial state has count0, point/worker points x0, starts/assignment indices/clock0, and a preselected uniform visited-iterate index; this does not change worker evolution.

Actual step restarts the just-completed worker and every worker whose new count minus its assignment index is at least R. This is the next-loop source stopping rule, applied at the same update boundary.

Actual step subtracts gamma times the received stochastic gradient, increments count, restarts the arriving worker at the new point and updates the actual clock. None replies leave state unchanged; the K guard prevents extra updates.

The actual descent providers retain coefficients -gamma/2 on current gradient, -gamma/4 on delayed gradient, gamma L squared/2 on the residual, and gamma squared L sigma squared/2 on noise. Expected_descent supplies the integrated form used by the telescoping argument.

The reused one-step descent statements assume the source step restriction gamma>0 and gamma<=1/(2L), causal delayed indices and actual stochastic-gradient moments. The time/iteration tuning implies these restrictions.
The actual residual_lemma bounds the average squared displacement by 1/(2 L squared (K+1)) times the delayed-gradient sum plus gamma sigma squared/L, preserving the source cancellation constants.

The actual residual theorem uses gamma<=1/(2RL) and bounded causal delay k-R<a_k<=k, as delivered by the stopping-rule invariant. No extra computation-model assumption is inserted into the analytic lemma.
Actual deadline_updates retains finite deadline_j as its premise and supplies all events before jR plus the jR clock bound. The new horizon R*j matches by commutativity without a changed constant.
Actual roundTime_mono has the correct direction: a later start cannot decrease the required completion deadline for nonnegative work.

Actual advance_ringmaster identifies every state component and the selected iterate under explicit answer/event-prefix equalities; delays_bound supplies bounded delay. Partial rules retain their hypotheses, and actual source calls are connected to successful updates only where events exist.

Actual iteration_bound gives 2Delta/(gamma(K+1))+2gamma L sigma squared; iteration_accuracy preserves arbitrary sufficient K and the original 8/16 bound. This is the analytic support for both source convergence results, not an extra advertised result.

Actual step_integral requires the appropriate measurable past dependence and integrability, then integrates the kth fresh sample independently. It is the explicit Fubini/tower step needed by the source proof.

Actual oracle_moments and iterate_moments yield the sigma squared plus true-gradient second-moment bound and measurable/integrable iterates, objective and gradient norms. Thus final integrals cannot exploit undefined nonintegrable expectations.

Actual noise_sum bounds the squared norm of the accumulated centered noise by interval length times sigma squared under the IID/causality assumptions; it does not assume mutually independent iterates.
